en: PHIVOLCS enforces a six-kilometer Permanent Danger Zone around Mayon Volcano to protect residents from sudden, deadly lava avalanches.
PAGASA issues Typhoon Wind Signal Number 5 to warn communities of expected winds exceeding 185 kilometers per hour.
Swimmers at Siargao Island must watch for strong rip currents that can quickly pull them away from shore.
The Philippine wet season creates stagnant water pools that serve as prime breeding grounds for dengue-carrying mosquitoes.
Coastal towns near the Philippine Trench need tsunami evacuation routes because undersea earthquakes can trigger massive waves.
Hikers climbing Mount Pulag must bring thick jackets because nighttime temperatures can drop below freezing and cause hypothermia.
Because the Philippines is near the equator, students must wear sunscreen daily to prevent sunburns from intense ultraviolet rays.
Residents in the mountainous Cordillera region must evacuate during heavy rains to avoid landslides triggered by saturated soil.
People living near Taal Lake must avoid drinking untreated water to prevent severe gastrointestinal illnesses from harmful bacteria.
Residents near erupting Taal Volcano must wear N95 masks to protect their lungs from inhaling hazardous volcanic ash.
During the dry season, Metro Manila's high heat index can cause heatstroke, so students must drink plenty of water.
Families near the Marikina River must monitor the water level alarm system to evacuate before dangerous flash floods occur.
